title: Add an urgent notice
prompt: `Notice` is supplied. Write `public class UrgentNotice : Notice` with a public get-only `int Hours` property and a public constructor `UrgentNotice(string title, int hours)` that stores both values. Its `public override string Label()` returns the title and hours, as in `"Storm (within 4 h)"`. It must also run through a `Notice` variable. Write `public static class Notices` with `public static List<string> Labels(List<Notice> notices)` returning every notice's `Label()` in order.
hints: Which constructor initializes the inherited Title, and which property belongs to UrgentNotice?
Pass title to the base constructor. Override Label rather than hiding it.
Use : base(title), assign Hours, and override Label. In Notices.Labels, loop over notices and call each Label().
support: static Notice AsNotice(string title, int hours) => (Notice)(object)new UrgentNotice(title, hours);
checks: Notices.Labels(new List<Notice> { new Notice("Rain"), AsNotice("Storm", 2) }).SequenceEqual(new List<string> { "Rain", "Storm (within 2 h)" })
checkLabels: An urgent notice's label must be its title and hours, as in "Storm (within 4 h)".
Calling Label through a Notice variable must still give the urgent text.
An urgent notice must keep its title.
Hours must hold the hours passed to the constructor.
Labels must return each notice's own label, in order.
An empty list must give an empty list.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Declares Label without override, so it only hides the base method.
Reads Title in the loop instead of calling Label().

feedback: If the label is right on an UrgentNotice variable but wrong through a Notice variable, check for the word override. Then check what Labels reads from each notice.
